neighbours.label: the short words fare, bare, dare, stare, spare, pare, hare, mare, ware(s) and the name Clare, in any sense, capitalised or not, and their forms (fares, dared, bared, staring, spared); quiet on the common '-are' words care, share, rare and square, on same-sound spellings (fair, pear, bear, hair), and on longer words that end in -are (welfare, nightmare, aware, compare, prepare, software)
fire: The bus fare went up by fifty cents this spring.
Nobody dared to open the old wooden door.
She stared at the map for a long time before deciding.
Do you have a spare pencil I could borrow?
The hare darted across the field and vanished into the hedge.
He walked barefoot along the cold sand.
Clare finished the crossword before breakfast.
The farmer led the grey mare back to the stable.
quiet: The bus ticket went up by fifty cents this spring.
Nobody wanted to share the old wooden desk.
She cared about the map more than the compass.
Do you have a square pencil case I could borrow?
The bear lumbered across the field and vanished into the hedge.
He walked along the cold sand in a nightmare of fog.
Claire's sister finished the crossword before breakfast.
The farmer led the grey horse back to the stable.

short: short '-are' words (fare, bare, dare, stare, spare...), not care/share/rare
predictions: most fire items above 0.4; care/share/square near misses below 0.2. Risks: 'barefoot' may tokenize differently, sentence-initial 'Clare'.
notes: Blind test: sentences written by a second author who saw only the label. Found as the top resident-attribution feeder of bonsai1/L2/N6869+ ('spare'); play step ran out of GPU memory, so no ablation drop was measured.
